subject: Procurement route & security gating — next steps and timeline

Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement route & security gating — next steps and timeline

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on procurement and security gating: 

- Procurement preference: you mentioned finance typically pays via PO for enterprise contracts but pilots sometimes go on card. Can you confirm which path you prefer for this initial production rollout?
- Security gating: you indicated SOC 2 and a signed DPA are firm requirements before data onboarding. We can provide a redacted SOC 2 and an editable DPA; Marissa (security) will outline evidence and timelines below.
- Marketplace: you asked whether we can do a faster purchase via the cloud marketplace — short answer: yes, that can reduce procurement friction but may change billing cadence and support entitlements. Ben, can you summarize marketplace vs PO trade-offs?

Proposed next steps: Emily to confirm procurement preference (PO vs card vs marketplace) and any internal procurement deadlines; Redwood to share SOC 2 redacted report and DPA draft; align on target signature/onboarding date.

Attachments: SOC2-Redwood-2024-redacted.pdf (redacted), DPA-Redwood-Acme-draft.docx (editable)

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement route & security gating — next steps and timeline

Thanks Tessa — good recap. A few clarifications from procurement/finance side: 

- For enterprise-wide rollouts we require a PO and 30-60 day payment terms. For initial pilots (limited scope, <3 months) we can accept card to get started faster, but we need a statement of work and fixed spend cap.
- SOC 2 (Type II) and a signed DPA are non-negotiable before any production data is processed. We can accept a redacted SOC 2 and an editable DPA for internal review.
- Marketplace: Procurement is open to marketplace purchases if the contract terms and SLAs match our requirements. Marketplace purchases would typically go through our procurement vendor team and can take slightly longer (~3–4 weeks to onboard) but simplify vendor onboarding.

Timeline constraints: Our vendor intake window for Q2 onboarding closes on 2027-03-15. If we want production before end of Q2, we need the signed DPA and evidence of SOC 2 before that date.

Happy to set a quick call with procurement if that helps.

Best,
Emily Zhang
Director, Clinical Data Platforms
Acme Health

Great — thanks Emily and procurement team. Looping in Ben (commercial ops) and Marissa (security) to propose concrete options and next steps.

Ben / Marissa: per Emily, key constraints are: PO preferred for enterprise rollout (30–60 day terms), card allowed for pilot with SOW/capped spend, marketplace acceptable but may take ~3–4 weeks. Vendor intake deadline: 2027-03-15 to hit Q2 onboarding.

Please advise: 
- Ben: short bullet list of PO vs card vs marketplace steps, typical lead times, and the minimal paperwork procurement will need from our side (SOW, W-9, master services agreement?). If we can provide a marketplace listing, will that materially shorten legal review?
- Marissa: what SOC 2 artifacts can we share immediately, and how long to assemble any additional evidence procurement may request? Also confirm whether our standard editable DPA is acceptable and whether an executed template via DocuSign would suffice for Acme.

Thanks — once we have these answers I’ll coordinate with Emily on target dates and a procurement kickoff if needed.

—Tessa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Procurement route & security gating — next steps and timeline

Hi all — quick summary from commercial ops and what I can prepare right away: 

PO route (enterprise rollout):
- Steps: send MSAs + SOW -> Acme legal review -> PO issuance -> onboarding.
- Typical lead time: 4–8 weeks depending on legal redlines.
- We can accept Net 30 or Net 45; Net 60 is possible with finance approval (may require sales credit hold).
- Paperwork we will provide: executed MSA template, SOW template, Redwood W-9, and invoice instructions.

Card route (pilot/faster):
- Steps: sign SOW + attach card to billing account -> immediate provisioning.
- Typical lead time: 1–5 business days once SOW is signed.
- Limitations: card billing means no PO on file; for a production rollout we’ll need a PO or marketplace contract later.

Marketplace route (accelerated vendor onboarding for some customers):
- Steps: customer purchases via Azure/AWS/GCP marketplace SKU -> marketplace vendor onboarding team handles some compliance checks -> contract flows through marketplace terms or a linked contract.
- Lead time: can be 2–4 weeks to show up in their procurement system but may simplify invoicing.
- Trade-offs: Support/SLA and refund terms may differ vs direct Redwood contract; legal still needs to confirm equivalence.

Attachments: procurement-options-PO-vs-marketplace.pdf (one-pager with timelines and required docs).

Marissa — can you confirm SOC 2 artifacts and whether DPA doc can be routed via DocuSign? If yes, Tessa / Emily — I suggest we aim to get the DPA signed by 2027-03-10 to hit the vendor intake window.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
